title: Previous-month NAO reduced Scotland winter rainfall test error in 1981-2025 under two linear response models
abstract: We tested whether previous-month North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) improves next-month winter rainfall predictions beyond recent local rainfall. The test used earlier winters to fit models and 135 test months per country in 1981-2025. Scotland log rainfall MSE fell by 10.26%, with a conditional 95% five-winter score-block interval of 4.60% to 16.30%. A raw rainfall model with a trend gave a 7.67% reduction, with limits of 2.38% to 13.36%. England and Wales gains remained uncertain. The original equal-country mean log gain was 4.43%, but its interval included zero when both models had a trend. A closer prior England and Wales test was found after initial scoring. We add Scotland and a log response check; the Scotland emphasis and raw model extension follow the initial results. This is an exploratory geographic extension, not independent confirmation. Revised data, assumed monthly input availability, country averages, model choice and conditional intervals limit the result. We include code, exact source paths and hashes, aggregate results, a figure and audit instructions. Source records and monthly derived tables remain outside the signed bundle.
